provenance.coverage_rulers_note: Three rulers describe this layer and all three are carried, not merged. (1) The scene DEC coverage header (verbatim below) states 39/39 elements; its own classes name 31 scene components plus the numbered non-component layers (word placements 2, audio 1, packaging 2, container 1) — a numbered sum of 37, with the script class 'recorded (cited)' carrying no number; the header's 39 does not decompose into its named classes anywhere in the record, and this package does not assert a derivation (the standing practice from migrations 5–6: carry the header verbatim, cite the enumerable ruler beside it, say the arithmetic is not decomposed). (2) The board audit (info.element) independently counts the same 39/39 from the same scene records — on this piece the second ruler AGREES with the header, unlike wd-02/wd-05. (3) The 2026-10-23 context audit counted 18/18 'elements' under a different, earlier element definition; it is cited as history, not as a competing count of the same set.

records.choice: The locked main audio, reassembled from its WAV sources (intro_audio + mastered content + outro_audio) — bit-identical programme to the delivered i2/i1 MP4, encoded to AAC exactly once at render (A-09). records.context: Final QC: WD −14.47 LUFS/TP −1.29, parity 1.55 dB; SOA −14.55/−1.20, parity 1.72 dB — re-verified on the v3 files in the build report.
records.why: The audio was never the defect; the caption drawer was.

records.choice: Words pop into the planned empty lower band (centres y=1290/1410, alternating), centred at x=530, DejaVu Sans Bold 62px, chalk; key words amber (the locked ACCENTS sets) with an overshoot pop. No plate, no band, no subtitle line anywhere in the DOM.
records.alternatives: The v2 caption plate (BANNED, V-16) and the fast-lane caption drawer (the overflow source).
records.context: QC V-16 + V-14 safe rect; reference @distribbapp word-animation short; Ep.2 v3 scene pattern.
records.why: The lower third is empty in every scene of both pieces by design — words live in the picture's negative space, timed to speech.
records.change: If a future scene's art fills the lower band, the bands move per-scene (DR per piece, as in Ep.2 v3).

records.choice: Phrases of at most 3 words; EVERY phrase group's rendered width is asserted at build time (PIL measurement of the embedded font) at ≤840px, and re-asserted on live DOM rects + rendered-frame pixel scans at QC. A failed assert stops the build.
records.alternatives: Trusting the drawer (the i2/i1 failure mode).
records.context: Final QC defect D-1 (WD L5 x 0–1018; SOA L5 x 0–1025, letters clipped by the frame edge itself).
records.why: R-03: a recurring defect indicts the workflow — the fix belongs in the template, not in one piece's numbers.
records.change: Nothing relaxes this; a wider group needs a smaller font, never a wider rect.

records.choice: faster-whisper word timestamps on the locked voice track, script words mapped via difflib (proto-v3 method, repairs logged in words.json); words arrive cumulatively inside a phrase, and a completed phrase HOLDS while the next phrase reveals, clearing when the phrase after next starts (C-05 carry-over, JOB DWELL-CONTRAST-FIX 2026-10-25).
records.alternatives: Whole-line captions (banned) and per-word karaoke over a standing line (a line on screen = subtitle).
records.context: QC V-16 timing rule; Ep.2 v3 alignment method; QC C-05 dwell floor (MEASURE-SWEEP 2026-10-25: the old clear-at-next-phrase rule left a median 0.20–0.51 s of full-visibility dwell against a 0.83 s floor).
records.why: At most two phrases (≤6 words) exist at any instant, in alternating bands; every word still arrives exactly with its spoken moment — only the completed phrase's clear moves.
records.change: Whisper boundary error >~150 ms on a re-alignment.

records.choice: The flagship container (Hadosh Academy intro, SUBSCRIBE outro, series header) rebuilt as HTML components on the same timeline — the MP4 is rendered from this file alone (H-01), so the container lives in the scene, not in a post-wrap. Header furniture moves inside the safe rect.

records.context: H-01; the v2 furniture at x≤1044/y≤104 was exempted from V-14 as container furniture in the final QC — v3 takes the stricter reading anyway.
records.why: One file = the whole video, container included; nothing readable sits outside the safe rect anymore.
records.change: A container redesign applies series-wide, not here.

accepted_exceptions_note: No accepted exception exists for this piece: the scene DEC block carries no exceptions structure, and the exceptions ledger (files/department-doc-anti-randomness.md §5, entries 1–11) names no wd-01 entry — its piece-named entries cover soa-01, eo-ep2-v3, wd-02, soa-05 and the DIR pair. Two class-level ledger entries touch this piece's kind without naming it: #7 (the sprint guide-voice-final rule — its timing superseded by the 2026-10-25 clone mandate; this piece's clone upgrade is that mandate executed) and #8 (fastlane finals mono against the P-04 stereo standard, accepted by Archer as a class disposition in craft-baseline CB-22 — this piece's delivered mono programme is exactly that deviation, recorded by the final QC as P-04). Following the practice of migrations 5–6, class-level entries are not instantiated as per-piece acceptances; the mono deviation itself is carried as a fact in audio/audio.json and render/verification.json. The field ships empty with this note because acceptances are revisable — a later erratum can reclassify an entry here without changing the file's shape (format rule from migration-2). The build's recorded deviations (the C-05 phrase-dwell carry-over inside DR-WORD-3; the wrapped_audio.wav mix-up caught at v3 QC inside DR-AUDIO) are decision records inside the DEC block, not accepted exceptions.
